security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel or M-mode firmware constructs ENTRY_CFG values without explicitly setting bit 2 (the now-baseline 'x' bit), causing the IOPMP to rely on the implementation-defined default for I/O device instruction-fetch permission to a protected memory region.
security_spec.summary: The x (instruction-fetch) bit in ENTRY_CFG moves from an optional X_PERM extension to the baseline spec at bit 2; kernel/firmware code that constructs ENTRY_CFG bitfields without setting bit 2 risks I/O devices executing from data-only regions because the hardware default for x is implementation-defined (WARL, DC).

findings.finding: These are clock gate definitions for IOPMP peripheral clocks on the TH1520 SoC. They control clock gating (enable/disable) for IOPMP-related bus clocks and have no involvement in constructing IOPMP ENTRY_CFG register values. No security-relevant entry permission configuration is performed here.
These are DT binding constant definitions for clock IDs used by the TH1520 clock driver. They are integer constants used in device tree, with no code that constructs IOPMP entry permissions.
Reset ID definition for the audio subsystem IOPMP reset line. No connection to IOPMP ENTRY_CFG or entry permission programming.
